questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The worst foods in Britain and why
How to become a chef in France
People who translate recipes into English
Why British vegetables are always overboiled
questions.why: Rob says they'll be meeting the recipe translators.

questions.q: What does Rob think about Britain's reputation for bad food?
options: It is completely true
It is no longer really true
It is only true in Scotland
It has never been true
questions.why: He says he doesn't think the reputation is still true, because of big changes in the last twenty years.

questions.q: What change in British eating does Rob describe?
options: Brits have started eating more black pudding
Brits now eat only French and Italian food
Brits are eating less food than they used to
Brits love international and vegan food now
questions.why: He says Brits have fallen in love with foods like Indian curry, Asian rice dishes and vegan food.

questions.q: What does a recipe translator need besides a dictionary?
options: Knowing ingredients and techniques
A restaurant of their own to test food
A degree in chemistry or biology
Experience as a food journalist
questions.why: Sam says they need to know vocabulary for ingredients and techniques while keeping the heart of the recipe.

questions.q: How did Rosa Llopis start her career?
options: As a chef in a Spanish restaurant
As a teacher of English in Madrid
As an interpreter at a cooking school
As a food writer for a newspaper
questions.why: She began working as an interpreter for Le Cordon Bleu, the French cuisine school.

questions.q: What did Rosa realise about Spain?
options: There were too many recipe translators
No one specialised in cooking translation
Spanish food wasn't popular abroad
Spanish recipes were too difficult
questions.why: She realised there was no such specialisation in gastronomy or cooking translation in Spain.

questions.q: Why does Rosa say readers must be able to replicate her recipes?
options: Otherwise they won't buy the book
Because her publisher requires it
So that restaurants can use them
Because the recipes are very old
questions.why: She says, 'If my readers can't replicate those recipes, they won't buy the book.'

questions.q: What does Rosa do when an ingredient is hard to find?
options: She removes the recipe from the book
She tells readers to buy it online
She leaves it out without explanation
She suggests a similar alternative
questions.why: She always tries to offer an alternative so readers can mimic the flavour or results.
